title: Expenses Incurred to-date by Singapore on High Speed Rail Project
what_it_is: Expenses Incurred to-date by Singapore on High Speed Rail Project

sections.label: HSR Project costs and Malaysia payments
sections.summary: Singapore incurred over S$270 million on the HSR Project and received about S$15 million from Malaysia for the 2018 suspension.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Singapore has incurred more than S$270 million for the Kuala Lumpur – Singapore High Speed Rail, or HSR Project.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Some of these costs, such as for consultancy services, design of infrastructure and manpower to deliver the HSR Project, are abortive costs if the HSR Project does not proceed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To date, Singapore has already received about S$15 million from Malaysia, arising from Malaysia’s request to suspend the construction of the HSR Project back in 2018 and up to May 2020.

sections.label: Malaysia termination compensation obligation
sections.summary: Under the Parties' agreement, Malaysia is obliged to pay termination compensation to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: According to the terms of the Parties' agreement, Malaysia is obliged to pay termination compensation to Singapore.

sections.label: Expenditure lower after suspension wind-down
sections.summary: Expenditure is roughly S$270 million, less than earlier indicated, because contracts were wound down and activity kept low during suspension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, our expenditure is roughly S$270 million, less than what he had indicated earlier, because when the Project was suspended and we agreed to the suspension, we wound down the contracts and we maintained activity at a low level, which is why we did not incur as much as it was indicated earlier.

sections.label: Amount cannot be disclosed
sections.summary: The amount cannot be disclosed due to confidentiality obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Unfortunately, due to confidentiality obligations, I cannot disclose the amount.

sections.label: Suspension extended to December 2020
sections.summary: The 2020 extension moved the suspension period to 31 December 2020, with the explicit understanding it was final.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The second, in 2020, extended the suspension period to 31 December 2020, with the explicit understanding that it would be the final extension.

sections.label: Malaysia proposed removing AssetsCo
sections.summary: The Parties could not agree to Malaysia's significant proposed change removing AssetsCo, the systems supplier and network operator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But we were unable to agree to one particularly significant change proposed by Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This involved the removal of the Assets Company – in short form, we call it "AssetsCo" – which is the systems supplier and network operator of the HSR service between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur (KL).

sections.label: HSR project suspensions and extensions
sections.summary: The Project was suspended two years to May 2020 at Malaysia's request, and a second extension to 31 December 2020 was agreed as final.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my earlier clarifications, at the request of Malaysia, we suspended the Project for two years up to May 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, there were two extensions, at the Malaysians' requests and we agreed to it in good faith and in the spirit of good bilateral relations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But we cannot extend indefinitely and, so, for the second extension to 31 December 2020, both sides agreed that it shall be the final extension, and it is part of the agreements.

sections.label: Groundbreaking and 2026 start
sections.summary: Johor Bahru has broken ground, Singapore will break ground soon, and both hope the Project and service commence in 2026 as scheduled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Johor Bahru side has broken ground; on our side, we will break ground soon and we hope the Project and the service can commence in 2026 as scheduled.

sections.label: Malaysia's KLIA HSR proposal
sections.summary: Malaysia's new proposal to connect the HSR to KLIA means the HSR will share tracks with the express rail link to KLIA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Having said that, Malaysia's new proposal to connect the HSR to Kuala Lumpur International Airport or KLIA means that HSR will share tracks with the express rail link to KLIA.

sections.label: Singapore-KL aviation route
sections.summary: Without the HSR, the Singapore-KL aviation route will continue carrying close to five million passengers, and the aviation hub status was not the key consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Since the Member has asked about the impact on aviation, actually, without the HSR, the Singapore-KL aviation route will continue to ferry and transport many passengers, in fact, closer to five million than the four million number stated by the Member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But throughout this whole discussion, the status of our aviation hub due to the HSR Project has not been the key consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We knew that this Singapore-KL air corridor is the busiest in the world – 46 flights a day, almost five million passengers a year – a number that is almost equivalent to Singapore's residential population.
